long_biography.plain_text:
For insurance executive Mike McGraw, premium volume mattered less than charging enough for the risk being accepted. At Pacific Specialty, he described a willingness to write less business when competitors drove prices below sustainable levels. That approach shaped a company selling specialist cover through independent agents, including insurance for motorcycles and personal watercraft.

His handling of technology reflected the same attention to how the business worked. Internet systems were offered to agents as another way to transact, while established methods remained available to those who preferred them. He regarded the agent's relationship with the customer as central, and wanted new tools to strengthen that relationship without dictating how every agent should work.
